summary: Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Oxford and the East India Company College, partly under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at the East India Company College (1844-1858) and served as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1860-1887).

Monika Boehm-Tettelbach worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, earning her doctorate under Heinz-Jürgen Pinnow at Free University of Berlin and habilitating at Bonn. Her main posts included professorships at Bamberg (~1989-1994) and Heidelberg (1990-2006).

Monika Zin is a scholar of Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Jagiellonian University, the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, and Munich. She held professorships at Munich (~2001-2016), Berlin (~2014-2015), and Leipzig (2017).
Moodeen Sheriff worked in Indology and medicine, having studied at Madras Medical College. He served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moriichi Yamazaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Tohoku University and Cambridge under Kenneth Roy Norman. He served as a professor at Sendai National College of Technology (~1987-2003) and president of Hosen Gakuen College (~2004).

Moritz Abraham Stern was a mathematician and linguist who studied at Heidelberg and Göttingen, where he was taught by Karl Otfried Müller. He spent his career at the University of Göttingen as an Extraordinarius from 1829 to 1884.

Moriz Haupt was a classical and Germanic philologist who studied under Gottfried Hermann at Leipzig. He served as professor at Leipzig (1841-1851) and Berlin (1853), and as perpetual secretary of the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1861-1874).

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Vienna under Georg Bühler and studied with Friedrich Max Müller. He held professorships at the German University in Prague (~1902-1934) and taught at Visva-Bharati University (1922-1924).

Morten Schlütter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Copenhagen, Komazawa, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He has held faculty posts at Victoria University of Wellington, Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist who studied at University College London under A. E. Housman. He directed the National Museum Wales (1920-1926), the London Museum (1926-1944), and served as Director-General of Archæology in India (1944-1948).

Morton Klass was an anthropologist who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University under Conrad M. Arensberg. He held faculty posts at Bennington College (1959), Barnard College (1965), and Columbia University (1982-1985).
Mother Sayamagyi was a religious and Buddhist studies teacher. She was a disciple of U Ba Khin, whom she eventually succeeded.

Motohiro Yoritomi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Motonobu Yoritomi, Gadjin M. Nagao, and Yuichi Kajiyama at Kyoto University. He was a longtime professor at Shuchiin University (1975-2011) and taught at Nichibunken (1998).

Motoi Ono is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Yasunori Ejima at the University of Tsukuba and earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna. Around 2002, he was appointed associate professor at the University of Tsukuba.

Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is an Indologist and philosopher. He served as a professor at Vidyasagar College (attested 1970-1975) and taught in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982-1994).

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He later held posts at the University of Leipzig (attested 2005) and the University of Heidelberg (attested 2007-2009).

Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. He has served as Deputy Director of the Taxila Museum, Director of Andhra Pradesh's Department of Archaeology and Museums, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).

Muhammad Nasim Khan is an archaeologist and linguist who earned his M.Phil at the University of Peshawar. He served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at Peshawar (attested 2006-2016) and held visiting affiliations with Hamburg and the Royal Asiatic Society.

Mukund Lalji Wadekar is an Indologist. He served as officiating director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 2002-2008) and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 2008), and general editor of the Gaekwad's Oriental Series.
Mukund Ram Shastri was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Head Pandit in the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1911 and 1916-1918).
